title: Hille–Yosida and contraction semigroups
subtitle: When an unbounded operator generates time evolution
adaptation: Mathematical companion outlining the definitions, argument, worked cases, and scope of the source lecture.

slides.title: From a generator to forward time
slides.lead: Heat flow loses energy; unitary flow preserves it.
body: A strongly continuous contraction semigroup acts for nonnegative time, satisfies the composition rule, and has norm at most one. A generator is its derivative at zero on the vectors where it exists.

slides.title: Dissipativity is the infinitesimal inequality
slides.lead: Every differentiable contractive trajectory starts with non-increasing norm.
body: Differentiate the squared norm along the trajectory at time zero. Dissipativity follows as a necessary condition on the generator.

slides.title: The range condition is essential
slides.lead: Dissipativity estimates solutions but does not create them.
body: For a densely defined closed operator, one needs (lambda I - G) to map its domain onto the whole space for some positive lambda. This makes the inverse everywhere defined.

slides.title: The resolvent bound
slides.lead: Contractivity is encoded in a reciprocal spectral estimate.
body: If y=(lambda I-G)^{-1}x, use dissipativity and Cauchy-Schwarz to get lambda||y||² <= ||x|| ||y||. The resolvent norm is therefore bounded by 1/lambda.

slides.title: Lumer–Phillips in Hilbert space
slides.lead: Maximal dissipativity characterizes contraction semigroup generators.
body: In the closed, densely defined case, dissipativity plus the full-range condition gives exactly the operator needed to generate a strongly continuous contraction semigroup.

slides.title: Hille–Yosida as a resolvent criterion
slides.lead: Every positive shift must admit a controlled inverse.
body: For a densely defined closed operator, the contraction-semigroup generation criterion asks for the entire positive real half-line in the resolvent set and uniform bounds on its powers.

slides.title: Bounded Yosida generators
slides.lead: Resolvent contractions lead to ordinary bounded exponentials.
body: Define J_lambda=lambda(lambda I-G)^(-1) and G_lambda=lambda(J_lambda-I). This generator is bounded and dissipative, so its exponential is a contraction for positive times.

slides.title: Construct the limiting semigroup
slides.lead: Control errors on the dense domain, then extend to all of H.
body: The Yosida generators converge on the original domain. A Duhamel comparison controls their exponentials on bounded time intervals. Contractivity lets the convergence extend to arbitrary input vectors.

slides.title: Heat equation: high modes decay faster
slides.lead: Dirichlet Laplacians provide concrete dissipative generators.
body: On the unit interval, the Dirichlet Laplacian has sine eigenmodes with eigenvalues -π²n². Each mode decays at that rate, and higher frequencies decay faster.

slides.title: Contrast groups and semigroups
slides.lead: Reversibility requires stronger symmetry than dissipativity.
body: A skew-adjoint generator defines a unitary group for both time directions. Maximal dissipativity generally supplies only a forward contraction semigroup; backward heat flow is not bounded on all L² data.
slides.takeaway: The sign of the generator decides whether high modes decay or grow.
